baslik: Hamas' Sneak Attack on Israel Deemed 'Major Failure' for Israeli Intelligence
metin:
On October 7, Palestinian militants from Gaza launched a surprise offensive called Operation Al-Aqsa Flood, firing thousands of missiles and advancing into Israeli territory. They infiltrated Israeli communities and military installations, capturing soldiers and equipment. The IDF responded with airstrikes on Gaza as casualties mounted. Prime Minister Netanyahu declared Israel 'at war.'

Dr. Meir Elran, retired IDF brigadier general, stated the attack began around 6:30 a.m. and 'caught the Israeli forces completely by surprise.' He acknowledged this represented a 'major blow both to the intelligence and to the operation of the IDF.' He called the incident a 'premeditated, pre-planned assault,' noting intelligence agencies failed to detect the preparations beforehand.

Dr. Simon Tsipis, a national security expert, called this 'probably one of the biggest failures' for Israel's internal security agency. He speculated the agency may have been misled by its own Gaza assets. Tsipis attributed the situation partly to Israel's political crisis, suggesting Netanyahu's government may have viewed war as its 'only chance to stay in power.' He noted reduced military readiness due to officer discontent and Hamas's financial support from Arab states.

Tsipis observed the Hamas operation was unprecedented in scale and coordination across multiple fronts. He characterized the current situation as a 'local clash' unlikely to escalate globally unless external actors like Hezbollah intervene.
